chunks: And from him, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said:

I asked him about salat (prayer) at night and during the day when the sun, the moon, and the stars cannot be seen. He said: Exercise your judgment, and deliberately face the qiblah to the best of your ability.

key_terms.اجْتَهِدْ: exert judgment and effort in determining the correct direction
key_terms.الشَّمْسُ: the sun, a natural sign used to determine direction
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer whose direction is being determined
key_terms.النَّهَارِ: daytime, indicating the ruling applies in both day and night
key_terms.النُّجُومُ: the stars, celestial markers for finding direction
key_terms.الْقَمَرُ: the moon, a celestial indicator for orientation
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةَ: the qiblah, the direction faced in salat (prayer)
key_terms.بِاللَّيْلِ: at night, referring to the time of prayer

ai.seo_question: What should a person do to determine the qiblah when the sun, moon, and stars are not visible?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who cannot determine the qiblah because celestial signs are not visible. It instructs the person to use personal effort and judgment to determine the direction of prayer as best as possible.
